sleep-screen-off.label: Put the phone away an hour before bed
sleep-screen-off.say: About an hour before bed, put the phone down somewhere out of reach and dim the lights — it tells your brain it's time to wind down. You can try it tonight.

sleep-warm-bath.label: A warm bath or shower before bed
sleep-warm-bath.say: A warm bath or shower an hour or two before bed helps — it's the cool-down afterward that makes you drowsy.

sleep-fixed-waketime.label: Get up at the same time every day
sleep-fixed-waketime.say: Get up at the same time every morning — weekends too. Your body clock resets from the morning end, and it usually takes about a week to feel the difference.

sleep-daylight-walk.label: Daylight and a walk during the day
sleep-daylight-walk.say: Get outside in the daylight and walk a little every day. It sounds too simple, but sunlight during the day is one of the best things for sleep at night — especially as we get older.

sleep-gentle-stretch.label: Gentle stretching before bed
sleep-gentle-stretch.say: A few slow stretches and some deep breaths before bed — let the shoulders and neck loosen up. It helps the whole body get the message that the day is over.

sleep-cut-caffeine.label: No caffeine after lunch
sleep-cut-caffeine.say: After lunch, skip the coffee, strong tea, and colas. Caffeine hangs around in your system a lot longer than most people think.

sleep-magnesium-food.label: Magnesium from food
sleep-magnesium-food.say: Leafy greens, nuts, beans, and bananas all have magnesium naturally. Getting it from food is the safest way — no worries about overdoing it.

sleep-magnesium-supplement.label: Magnesium before bed (supplement)
sleep-magnesium-supplement.dailyCap: No more than 350 mg a day from supplements (the U.S. safe upper limit)
sleep-magnesium-supplement.say: There's a fairly new study — done in adults who sleep poorly, like you — where taking magnesium before bed did ease insomnia a little. But the effect was small, and it doesn't work for everyone. If you try it, keep supplements at or under 350 mg a day — that's the U.S. safe limit, and more than that tends to cause diarrhea. And if you have kidney trouble or blood pressure issues, check with your doctor or pharmacist first.

sleep-split-rest.label: Sleep in two shifts
sleep-split-rest.say: If you know you'll be up in the night anyway, stop fighting it — plan your sleep in two blocks. Get a solid stretch in before they usually need you. It beats white-knuckling the whole night.

sleep-respite-service.label: Respite care so you can catch up on sleep
sleep-respite-service.say: Respite care means someone else takes over for a few hours so you can rest — and it's something you've earned, not a luxury. The Eldercare Locator at 1-800-677-1116 (weekdays) can point you to respite programs near you. Want me to remember that number for you?

sleep-melatonin-blocked.label: Melatonin — the honest picture
sleep-melatonin-blocked.say: Melatonin is sold over the counter here, but let me give you the honest picture: it works best for jet lag and a body clock that's off schedule. For plain chronic insomnia, the sleep doctors' own association actually recommends against it — the evidence just isn't there. And the bottles are messy: when researchers lab-tested store-bought melatonin, most had far more or less in them than the label said. I can't tell you to take it or how much — if you want to try it, talk to your pharmacist first, especially if you're on blood thinners or other medicines.

sleep-tcm-herbs.label: Herbal sleep remedies
sleep-tcm-herbs.say: Herbal sleep remedies aren't something I can pick out for you. One thing I do want you to know: 'natural' doesn't mean it can't clash with your medications — herbs can interact with prescriptions even if you take them hours apart, because both stay in your body for days. If you use anything herbal, make sure your doctor and your pharmacist both know about it.

sleep-refer-doctor.label: Time to see a doctor
sleep-refer-doctor.say: If this has gone on for a good while, or you're so tired it's affecting your days — or if you snore and seem to stop breathing in your sleep — that's worth a doctor visit. Start with your primary care doctor, and ask whether a sleep clinic makes sense.

knee-thigh-strength.label: Strengthen the thigh, not the knee
knee-thigh-strength.say: The most useful thing for bad knees isn't the knee — it's the thigh. Sit in a chair, straighten one leg out, hold it a few seconds, lower it. Then stand up and sit back down holding the chair back. A few times a day is plenty. Strong thigh muscles carry the load so the knee doesn't have to.

knee-weight.label: Weight makes the biggest difference
knee-weight.say: Every pound you take off comes off that knee several times over with each step — it's the plainest arithmetic in this whole subject, and the evidence behind it is far stronger than anything sold in a supplement bottle.

knee-avoid-squat.label: Steer around what wears the knee down
knee-avoid-squat.say: Walk on flat ground, take the elevator where there is one, and stay out of deep squats and kneeling. The chores that put you down on the floor — scrubbing, reaching into low cabinets — do those sitting down or with a long-handled tool.

knee-patch.label: Pain patches and rubs
knee-patch.say: A patch or a rub to take the edge off for an evening is perfectly fine. What I'd steer you away from is using one every day for months to keep the problem quiet — pain is the body talking, and it's worth hearing what it's saying.

knee-glucosamine.label: Glucosamine and chondroitin
knee-glucosamine.dailyCap: Follow the product label, and don't double up with another product containing the same ingredient
knee-glucosamine.say: Honest answer on glucosamine and chondroitin: the research is middling to weak and plenty of people feel nothing at all. You can try it — just don't make it your main plan. What genuinely works here is weight and thigh strength. **And if you're on a blood thinner, your kidneys aren't in good shape, or you're allergic to shellfish, ask your doctor or pharmacist before you start** — a lot of glucosamine is made from shellfish.

knee-surgery-blocked.label: Surgery and injections
knee-surgery-blocked.say: Whether to have surgery, and whether to get a cortisone or hyaluronic acid injection, is the orthopedist's judgment. I won't make that decision for you.

knee-refer.label: When it isn't ordinary wear and tear
knee-refer.say: If one knee suddenly swells, feels hot to the touch, and you're running a fever — or you couldn't put weight on it after a fall or a knock — that isn't ordinary wear and tear. Get it looked at promptly so a doctor can rule out an infection or a fracture.

bp-take-meds-on-time.label: Same time every day, no adjusting on your own
bp-take-meds-on-time.say: The single biggest thing with blood pressure pills: same time every day, no skipping, no doubling up on your own. Keep them somewhere you can't miss — next to the toothbrush, or by the coffee maker.

bp-measure-right.label: How to take your blood pressure right
bp-measure-right.say: Sit and rest for five minutes first, keep your arm at heart level, and check at the same time of day each time. Readings naturally bounce around during the day — a sloppy reading just gives you a scare for nothing.

bp-reduce-salt.label: Ease up on the salt
bp-reduce-salt.say: For most Americans the salt isn't in the shaker — it's in canned soups, deli meats, frozen dinners, bread, and restaurant food. Cutting back there, and going easy on the sauces, does more than anything else you can do in the kitchen.

bp-dash-diet.label: The DASH way of eating
bp-dash-diet.say: The DASH diet — plenty of vegetables and fruit, whole grains, low-fat dairy — was designed specifically for blood pressure, and the research behind it is solid. One caution: if your kidneys aren't in good shape, don't load up on potassium-rich foods without asking your doctor first.

bp-walk.label: A regular walk
bp-walk.say: A brisk half-hour walk, five days a week, genuinely moves the needle on blood pressure. You don't have to start there — ten minutes counts.

bp-stress-sleep.label: Stress and bad sleep push it up too
bp-stress-sleep.say: Stress, poor sleep, and sudden cold snaps can all send your numbers up for a while — it doesn't always mean the medicine stopped working. First ask yourself: has this been an especially rough week?

bp-normalize.label: You're in very common company
bp-normalize.say: More than half of Americans over 65 — closer to two out of three — have high blood pressure. It's the most common chronic condition there is. This isn't something you did wrong.

bp-med-change-blocked.label: Changing your medication
bp-med-change-blocked.say: Switching, adding, or stopping blood pressure medicine is your doctor's call, not mine — and I don't interpret your readings either. What I can do is help you keep track of them to show your doctor.

bp-refer.label: When it's an emergency
bp-refer.say: If your top number reads over 180, or you notice a drooping face, a weak arm, or slurred speech (signs of stroke), or chest pressure with a cold sweat (signs of a heart attack) — call 911 right away. Don't wait for your next appointment.

bp-salt-substitute-caution.label: Salt substitutes aren't for everyone
bp-salt-substitute-caution.say: Salt substitutes do cut the sodium roughly in half, and for most people that's a sensible trade. **But they work by swapping in potassium — and kidneys that aren't in good shape can't clear it. Too much potassium leaves you weak all over and can throw the heart rhythm off.** Some blood pressure medicines raise potassium on their own too: the -pril and -sartan ones, and spironolactone. **So if you have any kidney trouble, or you're on blood pressure pills, ask your doctor or pharmacist before you switch shakers.** The safest way to cut back on salt isn't a different shaker anyway — it's garlic, onion, lemon, vinegar, black pepper and the salt-free herb blends.

bp-potassium-foods.label: Where to get potassium, magnesium and calcium — and how strong the evidence is
bp-potassium-foods.say: The reason everyone tells you to eat more produce is the potassium — it helps the body shed extra sodium. The evidence holds up reasonably well: pooling dozens of trials, people who already have high blood pressure and add potassium drop the top number by about 4 to 5 points. Not huge, but consistent — and **the people who gain most are the ones who were eating a lot of salt and very little produce**. Easy sources: bananas, potatoes with the skin, sweet potatoes, spinach, tomatoes, beans, lentils, oranges, cantaloupe, plain yogurt. Magnesium is in dark greens, nuts and whole grains; calcium in milk, yogurt, tofu, canned sardines. You don't need to overhaul anything — start with one extra vegetable at each meal and one piece of fruit a day. One important exception: **if your kidneys aren't working well, or you take a medicine that raises potassium, check before adding any of this.** Too much potassium is dangerous.

bp-isometric-exercise.label: Isometric exercise — wall sits and hand grip (newer evidence, and not a small effect)
bp-isometric-exercise.say: Here's something that surprised a lot of people. Exercise where you hold force without moving — a wall sit, or squeezing a grip — lowers blood pressure more than walking does. Pooling around 270 trials, that category averaged an 8.2 point drop; walking came in around 4 to 5. The protocol is four sets of 2 minutes of effort with 2 minutes rest between, three days a week, with results showing by 8 to 10 weeks. Aim for "working, but I could hold this." An older-adult version: back against the wall, one step forward with the feet, bend the knees only slightly, hold 2 minutes. If standing is unsteady, do it seated — hold a towel at both ends and pull outward, or just grip the towel hard, 2 minutes. **The one rule that matters: keep breathing normally the whole time. Never hold your breath.** Stop for dizziness or headache.

bp-weight-alcohol.label: What weight, alcohol and coffee are each worth
bp-weight-alcohol.say: Three things move blood pressure directly. Here are the numbers. **Weight** — roughly 1 point off the top number per kilogram (about 2 pounds) lost. Five kilos is 4 to 5 points, about what one medication does. **Alcohol** — there's a threshold here. If you're already at two drinks a day or fewer, quitting barely moves your blood pressure. But **if you're drinking more than two a day, cutting the amount in half drops the top number by 5 to 6 points on average** — for heavy drinkers this is the best-value move in the whole topic. **Coffee** — regular drinkers see little effect, so there's no need to quit. But someone who doesn't normally drink it can spike about 10 points for a while after a cup, so don't drink coffee in the 30 minutes before you measure.

bp-food-remedies.label: Food remedies — what has something behind it and what's just comforting
bp-food-remedies.say: Let me sort the strong from the weak honestly. Two have something behind them. **Hibiscus tea** — pooled studies show roughly a 5 to 7 point drop in the top number, though the trials vary a lot. Unsweetened, two or three cups a day, it's a fine daily drink. **Garlic** — used in cooking, people with high blood pressure may see a few points. On the other side: celery juice, apple cider vinegar, onion soaked in wine, beet-and-cucumber detox drinks — there isn't decent human research supporting "this lowers blood pressure." Enjoy them as food. But **don't let them replace medication, and never skip a dose because you drank something** — that's the dangerous part. And if your pressure is running low enough to make you lightheaded on your medication, don't adjust it yourself; call the office.

bp-supplements-honest.label: Are supplements worth it? (Mostly not)
bp-supplements-honest.dailyCap: EPA + DHA under 2 g a day, total fish oil under 3 g. Aged garlic extract 600 to 1200 mg
bp-supplements-honest.say: I've run the numbers on this one. For blood pressure specifically, most supplements aren't a good buy. **CoQ10** — the pooled review found no clear effect on blood pressure. That's money you can keep. **Fish oil** — about 2.5 points on the top number, which is very small. It has other cardiovascular arguments, but don't buy it to lower blood pressure. Keep labeled EPA + DHA under 2 grams a day and total under 3. **Beetroot juice** — around 3.5 points short-term; whether it holds across a full day isn't well established. The strongest of the bunch is **aged garlic extract**, averaging about 8 points in people with high blood pressure — comparable to walking. Typical dose 600 to 1200 mg a day. If you're on a blood thinner or have surgery coming, clear concentrated garlic and fish oil with your doctor first.

bp-herb-drug-clash.label: The things that fight with blood pressure medication
bp-herb-drug-clash.say: A few things collide with the medications. **Red yeast rice** — it naturally contains the same compound as prescription cholesterol drugs, so taking both risks muscle breakdown. Don't stop either on your own; take both bottles to the pharmacist. **Licorice** — not the candy flavoring, but real licorice root, licorice tea and licorice-containing herbal formulas. Used regularly it makes the body hold sodium and dump potassium, and blood pressure climbs. It takes about ten days to come back down after stopping. **Decongestants** — pseudoephedrine and phenylephrine in cold and sinus products tighten blood vessels and push both pressure and pulse up. Say "I have high blood pressure" before you buy anything over the counter. **NSAIDs** — ibuprofen, naproxen and the like. Taken regularly they raise blood pressure and blunt your medication.

dm-veggie-first.label: Change the order you eat
dm-veggie-first.say: Eat your vegetables and protein first, and save the bread, potatoes, or rice for last. Same meal, different order — your blood sugar climbs more gently. You can start at dinner tonight.

dm-carb-swap.label: Swap half the white stuff
dm-carb-swap.say: Swap half of the white bread, white rice, and regular pasta for whole wheat, brown rice, oatmeal, or sweet potatoes. That beats any miracle diet you'll see on TV.

dm-walk-after-meal.label: A short walk after meals
dm-walk-after-meal.say: Fifteen or twenty minutes of walking after a meal makes a real, well-documented difference to after-meal blood sugar. No need to hurry — a stroll counts.

dm-sugary-drinks.label: Cut the sugary drinks first
dm-sugary-drinks.say: Soda, sweet tea, fruit juice, sports drinks — sugar you drink hits the bloodstream fastest of all. Cutting just this one thing changes the numbers for a lot of people.

dm-take-meds.label: Stay steady with meds and checkups
dm-take-meds.say: Take your medicine on schedule and don't put off your checkups. Blood sugar is a long game — stopping and starting is what does the most damage.

dm-normalize.label: You're far from alone
dm-normalize.say: Nearly three in ten Americans over 65 have diabetes. It's one of the most common conditions of getting older — not a sign you didn't take care of yourself.

dm-med-blocked.label: Adjusting doses or reading your numbers
dm-med-blocked.say: I don't interpret blood sugar readings, and adjusting your medicine is strictly your doctor's call. Whether a supplement is safe alongside your diabetes medicine — that's a question for your pharmacist.

dm-refer.label: When to get help fast
dm-refer.say: **Low blood sugar is the most urgent thing here**: a cold sweat and shakiness, but still awake and able to swallow — take glucose tablets, juice, or regular (not diet) soda right away. **And remember the second half: if they become confused or you can't wake them, call 911 immediately** — these two things always go together, never just the first part. Already confused or unresponsive means 911, now. Also: extreme thirst, confusion, and rapid breathing with fruity-smelling breath means get medical help immediately — and a sore or cut that just won't heal needs a doctor's look.

dm-carb-exchange.label: You can eat rice and bread — the question is how much
dm-carb-exchange.say: The most important sentence first: **it isn't that you can't eat carbs, it's how much.** Dietitians count in carb servings, and one serving is 15 grams of carbohydrate. In things you can see: a third of a cup of cooked rice or pasta is one serving, so a full cup is about three. One slice of bread is one serving. Half a cup of cooked potato, sweet potato, corn, peas or beans is one. A small tortilla is one; a large flour tortilla can be three. Here's where most people get caught: **potatoes, sweet potatoes, corn, peas, winter squash and beans are on the starch side of the plate, not the vegetable side.** On a day you eat those, take the rice or bread down accordingly. Cut in this order: sugary drinks first, then the starch portion. Don't cut the vegetables or the protein.

dm-exercise-rx.label: The exercise prescription — 150 minutes a week, plus strength twice or three times
dm-exercise-rx.say: Here's a version you can actually follow. **150 minutes a week of moderate aerobic activity**, spread over at least three days. Don't go two days in a row without any — the benefit fades in that gap. Moderate means you're breathing harder and sweating a little but can still talk in full sentences. If you could sing, it's too easy. Brisk walking, cycling, swimming, dancing all count. **Strength work twice or three times a week**, never two days back to back — the muscle rebuilds on the off day. No gym required: stand up from a chair and sit back down, 10 reps a set, two or three sets. Resistance band pulls. Water bottles as weights. Half squats holding the chair back. This is the piece that helps blood sugar most. Even a **10-minute walk 30 to 60 minutes after eating** flattens the after-meal spike noticeably.

dm-exercise-meds.label: On insulin or certain pills? A few extra steps around exercise
dm-exercise-meds.say: If you take insulin, or a pill that pushes your body to make insulin (your pharmacist can tell you which), exercise needs a few extra moves. **Don't exercise on an empty stomach**, especially right after a dose. The classic setup for trouble is a pre-dawn walk with breakfast afterward. **Carry sugar.** Glucose tablets or a small juice box in the pocket. Not chocolate, not cookies — the fat slows absorption and it won't rescue you in time. Don't head somewhere remote alone. Tell whoever you walk with: "I have diabetes. If I start acting strange or slurring, give me sugar first." A card in your wallet with your name, condition, doctor and an emergency contact is worth doing.

dm-hypo-1515.label: Low blood sugar — how to spot it, the 15-15 rule
dm-hypo-1515.say: Lows come on fast. The classic signs are sudden cold sweat, shaky hands, racing heart, dizziness, ravenous hunger, going pale. Older adults often don't get those — instead they get **suddenly exhausted, slurred or muddled speech, slowed movements, or irritable**. Families usually read it as a bad mood. That's the mistake. If the person is awake and can swallow, use 15-15. Take **15 grams of fast sugar**: 3 to 4 glucose tablets, 4 ounces of juice, 5 ounces of regular soda, a tablespoon of sugar or honey, or a few hard candies. Wait 15 minutes, recheck if there's a meter. Still low or still feeling it — repeat the same amount. **One critical exception**: if they take an alpha-glucosidase inhibitor (acarbose, miglitol), **table sugar won't work fast enough — it has to be glucose tablets or gel.** Anyone on those should carry glucose. If they're not fully alert or can't swallow, **put nothing in their mouth and call 911**.

dm-fruit.label: Fruit isn't off the table — two servings a day, and don't drink it
dm-fruit.say: You can eat fruit, and you should — the fiber, potassium and vitamins earn their place. It's about amount and form. **Two servings a day.** One serving is about the size of your fist, or a small bowl of cut fruit: one small apple, one medium orange, half a large banana, about 15 grapes, a cup of berries, a cup of melon. So one large banana is two servings — that's your fruit for the day. Two things matter most. **Don't juice it and don't buy juice** — the fiber is gone, the sugar arrives much faster, and a glass is usually three or four pieces of fruit that you drink in a minute. Eat it whole, and chew. And **split it up** — one serving in the morning, one in the afternoon. All at once will spike you. Many people find it goes down better as a between-meal snack than right on top of a meal.

dm-folk-food.label: Bitter melon, cinnamon, apple cider vinegar, okra water — one at a time
dm-folk-food.say: Let me go through the ones people ask about most, honestly. **Bitter melon** — pooled international trials found no measurable blood sugar advantage over placebo or over diabetes medication, and the trials were low quality. A 2023 review put it plainly: current evidence can't tell. So — **excellent as a vegetable** (high fiber, low calorie, good as the first thing on your plate) but not as a treatment. **Cinnamon** — results scatter widely; pooled, the effect is small or unclear. Fine in cooking, not worth buying for. **Apple cider vinegar** — small studies suggest a modest effect on after-meal glucose, but nothing that would change your medication. It's also hard on tooth enamel undiluted. **Okra water** — no meaningful human evidence at all. One thing worth knowing about labels: **"supports healthy blood sugar" is a structure/function claim, not an FDA-approved treatment claim** — the fine print says so on the bottle.

dm-supplement-truth.label: How to read supplements — the caps, who shouldn't, what isn't worth buying
dm-supplement-truth.dailyCap: Chromium: diet supplies the small amount needed (about 25 to 35 mcg). Products often exceed 200 mcg and no long-term safe upper limit is set
dm-supplement-truth.say: The most useful sentence first: **nothing marketed for blood sugar replaces medication, and most do less than you think.** That money buys better groceries and a decent pair of shoes. **Chromium** — the American Diabetes Association doesn't recommend it, because studies haven't confirmed a benefit in diabetes. The body needs very little, and normal eating supplies it. Bottles routinely hold 200 mcg or more per capsule, and no safe long-term upper limit has been established — meaning nobody really knows. **Alpha-lipoic acid** — some evidence for nerve pain symptoms, but it isn't a glucose-lowering product. **Berberine** — this one does lower glucose in small studies, which is exactly why it isn't harmless: **stacked on diabetes medication it can drop you too low**, and it interacts with a long list of drugs. Common rule for all of them: add only one thing at a time, and tell the doctor who manages your diabetes that you're starting it.

dm-foot-care.label: Look at the feet daily, get them checked yearly
dm-foot-care.say: After years of high glucose the nerves in the feet go quiet — you can break the skin and not feel it — and circulation is poorer, so it heals slowly. Most amputations start with a small wound nobody noticed. **One thing daily**: after your shower, sit down and look at both feet — soles, heels, both sides, every space between the toes. Put a mirror on the floor if you can't bend; ask family if your eyesight isn't up to it. You're looking for breaks, blisters, red spots, color changes, soggy skin between toes. **Test bath water with your elbow**, not your foot. Dry thoroughly, especially between the toes. Lotion on the top and sole, never between the toes. Don't do these yourself: no razor blades or graters on calluses or corns, no medicated corn pads, no heating pad left on your feet overnight. And **have your feet examined at least once a year**.

dm-annual-checks.label: The yearly checks — write them on a card and hand it over
dm-annual-checks.say: Blood sugar isn't just the fingertip number. There's a short list that should happen on a schedule, and it's the part most often missed. The basics: **A1c at least twice a year**. **A lipid panel yearly.** **Urine albumin yearly** — that's the early warning for the kidneys. **A foot exam at least yearly.** And **a dilated eye exam yearly** — diabetic eye damage has no symptoms early on, and by the time vision changes it's often advanced. What to do today: write those five on a card and hand it to your doctor at the next visit with one question — "which of these have I had this year?" Have them write the dates on the card and you can reuse it next year.

gout-avoid-triggers.label: These are the usual fuses
gout-avoid-triggers.say: Organ meats, shellfish, rich meat broths and gravies, and alcohol — beer most of all. During a flare, cut all of them out. Those are the ones that set most people off.

gout-water.label: Keep the water going
gout-water.say: Drinking water through the day helps flush uric acid out — spread it across the daytime rather than all at once. **And if your doctor has told you to limit fluids — with heart failure, or if you're on dialysis — their instructions beat mine every time.**

gout-sugary-drinks.label: Sweet drinks are a culprit too
gout-sugary-drinks.say: Here's the one most people don't know: drinks sweetened with fructose — soda, sweet tea, fruit punch, juice — push uric acid up about as much as beer does. That's the first thing worth cutting.

gout-weight.label: Lose weight slowly, not fast
gout-weight.say: Losing weight usually brings uric acid down along with it — but it has to be slow. Crash dieting can actually set off an attack, which is the opposite of what you wanted.

gout-lemon-soda.label: Lemon water and baking soda
gout-lemon-soda.say: Lemon water and baking soda for gout are folk remedies — the evidence is thin. No harm in the lemon water if you like it, but don't treat it as a cure, and don't let it talk you out of avoiding the things that actually set you off. Baking soda in particular is loaded with sodium, so go easy on that one if you have blood pressure or heart trouble.

gout-med-blocked.label: Uric acid pills and painkillers
gout-med-blocked.say: I can't tell you doses for uric acid medicine or anti-inflammatory painkillers. And if you take a water pill, whether it's feeding your gout is a question for your doctor — those two are connected more often than people realize.

gout-refer.label: When it might not be gout at all
gout-refer.say: If that joint is red, hot, swollen and painful **and** you have a fever — or the pain is spreading and getting worse — get seen promptly. That combination can be an infection in the joint or in the skin rather than gout, and it isn't something to ice at home and wait out.

consti-water.label: Water first
consti-water.say: A lot of folks cut back on water because they don't want to be running to the bathroom — and then things get harder to pass. Fiber can't do its job without water behind it. Sip through the day instead of waiting until you're thirsty.

consti-fiber-food.label: Fiber from the table
consti-fiber-food.say: Leafy greens, sweet potatoes, fruit with the skin on, beans, and swapping half your white bread or rice for whole grain. Fiber from food is the real article — just make sure the water comes along with it.

consti-kiwi-prune.label: Kiwifruit or prunes
consti-kiwi-prune.say: Two kiwifruit a day, or a handful of prunes. Of all the foods people swear by for this, those two are among the few that actually hold up when they're studied.

consti-routine.label: Same time every morning
consti-routine.say: Your bowel is most willing about half an hour after breakfast. Go sit at that time each day, unhurried, whether or not you feel much urge — over a few weeks the body picks up the rhythm.

consti-walk.label: Get up and move
consti-walk.say: Sit still all day and the bowel gets lazy right along with you. A ten- or fifteen-minute walk after a meal is the cheapest thing on this whole list.

consti-probiotics.label: Probiotics
consti-probiotics.dailyCap: Follow the label; don't take several similar products at the same time
consti-probiotics.say: You can try a probiotic, but the strains differ enormously and plenty of people feel nothing — the evidence is nowhere near as solid as 'enough water plus enough fiber.' Don't let it be your main plan. **And if your immune system is compromised, you're in chemotherapy, or you've had a large part of your bowel removed, ask your doctor before you take one.**

consti-laxative-blocked.label: Laxatives and enemas
consti-laxative-blocked.say: I won't pick a laxative, a stool softener, or an enema for you, or tell you how much to use. And leaning on a laxative long term makes the bowel lazier still — that's a conversation for your doctor, not something to sort out at the drugstore shelf.

consti-refer.label: When it needs a doctor
consti-refer.say: If there's blood in your stool or it's turned black, if you're losing weight without trying, or if you've gone from regular to nothing at all with bad belly pain — that's a doctor's visit, promptly. Changing your diet won't fix that kind.  If there's trouble breathing, confusion, or pain you can't bear, don't wait — call 911.

consti-fiber-slow.label: Add fiber slowly — and it doesn't work for everyone
consti-fiber-slow.say: Add fiber a little at a time, week by week. Deciding today and eating vegetables all day usually buys you bloating and gas, and then you quit. Give it four to six weeks, and bring the water up alongside it. And something honest: **fiber doesn't work for everyone.** If adding it makes you more bloated or crampy, or you feel the urge but still can't pass anything, the problem may not be "not enough roughage" — it may be a slow-moving colon or an outlet that isn't relaxing. That needs a doctor. More fiber will just make you miserable.

consti-psyllium.label: Psyllium husk — how to take it, how much water, how far from your pills
consti-psyllium.dailyCap: Start at 5 g a day, build to around 10 g. Always with a full glass (8 oz or more) of water
consti-psyllium.say: Psyllium husk is the pharmacy fiber that actually has clinical trials behind it, which is rare in this aisle. How to take it: **start at 5 grams**, after breakfast, mixed into a full 8-ounce glass of water and drunk right away — don't let it sit and thicken. Build to about 10 grams, split morning and evening. Four rules. **One: without enough water it can congeal in the throat or gut, and that is genuinely dangerous.** **Two: keep it two hours away from your other medications** — it blocks absorption. **Three: not for anyone with swallowing difficulty, or a history of bowel obstruction or narrowing.** **Four: not a good fit for someone bedbound who can't take that much fluid.** Expect a few gassy days at the start; it usually settles.

consti-posture.label: How you sit on the toilet — put a low stool under your feet
consti-posture.say: You can change the position. Put a stool about 8 inches high under your feet so the knees sit higher than the hips, lean forward, elbows on thighs. That straightens the bend in the rectum and takes some of the work out of it. Two things matter more than the stool. **Don't hold your breath and bear down** — straining spikes blood pressure, which matters for older adults. And **don't sit longer than 10 minutes**. Leave the phone outside. Long sits are how hemorrhoids happen. If nothing comes, get up and wait for the next urge. Honestly: the stool has measurable benefit in healthy volunteers, but randomized trials in people who are actually constipated haven't shown a clear difference. It's free to try — and if it does nothing, that's not your fault.

consti-massage.label: Abdominal massage — direction, timing, how long
consti-massage.say: You can do this yourself or for someone you care for, and **the direction matters — clockwise**: up from the lower right, across under the ribs, down the left side. That traces the path of the colon. Timing is 30 to 60 minutes after a meal, with a warm flat hand, firm enough to feel it but never painful, 5 to 10 minutes at a time, once or twice a day. The evidence is moderate — randomized trials show more bowel movements and less bloating, but the studies are small. What it has going for it: it's safe, free, and the person doing it can talk with the person receiving it. Skip it after abdominal surgery, over a wound, or if pressing hurts.

consti-drug-cause.label: A lot of constipation is caused by medication
consti-drug-cause.say: Here's what almost nobody is told: **a lot of constipation is the medication, not the bowel.** The usual suspects — opioid pain medicines above all, plus ordinary anti-inflammatories; iron tablets; calcium supplements; aluminum-containing antacids; some blood pressure medicines, especially calcium channel blockers; antidepressants; sedatives and sleep aids; cough medicines; antihistamines. If this started recently, think back to what was added recently. The timing usually lines up. **But don't stop anything on your own** — every one of those was prescribed for a reason. What to do: put every medication and supplement in one bag, take it to the doctor or pharmacist, and ask directly: "Is anything in here likely to be causing this, and is there an alternative?"

consti-elder-causes.label: In older adults it's usually several causes stacked together
consti-elder-causes.say: Constipation in an older adult is rarely one thing. Go through them one at a time. **Teeth or dentures don't work, so vegetables are out** and it's soft rice and something salty. That gets fixed at the dentist, or by chopping, cooking soft, or blending into soup. Telling them to eat more vegetables won't do it. **Afraid of nighttime trips or needing help, so they drink nothing all day.** Move the fluids to daytime, prompt at set times, and check whether the bathroom is simply too far or unsafe at night. **Sitting or lying down all day** — the bowel slows with the body. Underactive thyroid, diabetes and Parkinson's all slow things down too. If it's gotten gradually worse over a year or two, with feeling cold and unusually tired, mention it — a blood test answers that.

consti-coffee.label: A morning cup of coffee (it genuinely works for some people)
consti-coffee.say: A hot coffee in the morning really does work for some people — studies measure a clear increase in colon contractions, roughly on par with eating a meal. Decaf works too, so it isn't purely the caffeine. Use it simply: a cup with breakfast, paired with the earlier advice about sitting on the toilet 30 minutes after eating. Two cautions. If you also have heartburn or reflux, coffee may make you feel worse — skip this one. And **coffee doesn't count as water**. Drink the water anyway.

consti-fruit-honest.label: Kiwi, prunes, bananas, honey — what actually holds up
consti-fruit-honest.say: Ranked by how good the evidence is. The strongest are **kiwifruit and prunes** — those have real trials behind them. Two kiwis a day, or five or six prunes. **Pears, apples and berries** are sensible choices on fluid and fiber, but there isn't much research done directly in constipated people — call them reasonable, not proven. **Yogurt** depends entirely on the strain; that's a separate conversation. **Bananas and honey water** deserve lowered expectations — underripe bananas can actually make things harder, and honey water is mostly comfort. One thing people don't know: **prunes, apples and pears carry sorbitol, and too much means gas and loose stools. One serving a day** — don't dose them like medicine.

keywords: feeling dizzy when I stand up

dizzy-two-step.label: Stand up in two stages
dizzy-two-step.say: Stand up in two stages: sit up first, wait a few seconds, then rise slowly. Getting out of bed, sit on the edge for a moment before you stand. You can start tonight — and it's the single most effective thing.

dizzy-hydrate.label: Drink enough water, don't stand too long
dizzy-hydrate.say: Hot days, too little water, and alcohol all make it worse. Keep the water coming, and avoid standing still in one spot for long stretches.

dizzy-explain.label: What's actually happening
dizzy-explain.say: This is called orthostatic hypotension — you change position, your blood pressure doesn't catch up fast enough, and the brain runs short for a moment. It's very common in older adults, and just knowing what it is takes some of the scare out.

dizzy-med-review.label: Mention it at your next appointment
dizzy-med-review.say: Blood pressure pills and water pills are common culprits. At your next visit, tell your doctor 'I get dizzy when I stand up' and let them decide whether to adjust anything — **but never stop a medication on your own**.

dizzy-fall-proof.label: Clear the fall hazards while you're at it
dizzy-fall-proof.say: Dizzy spells and falls travel together. A night light on the path to the bathroom, a non-slip mat in the shower, no loose rugs or clutter in the hallway — small stuff that prevents big trouble.

dizzy-refer.label: When it's an emergency
dizzy-refer.say: **If dizziness comes with weakness on one side, a drooping face, slurred speech, a sudden terrible headache, or double vision — those are stroke signs. Call 911 immediately.** And if the spells keep coming back, or you've already had a fall, have your doctor take a look.

eye-light-safety.label: Light the house properly
eye-light-safety.say: When you can't see well, the real danger is falling. Turn the lighting up at home, leave a light on at the stairs and in the hallway, and keep the things you use every day in the same spot so you're not hunting for them.

eye-uv.label: A hat and sunglasses
eye-uv.say: Ultraviolet light speeds cataracts along. A hat and a pair of sunglasses when you go out — cheap, easy, and it genuinely helps.

eye-food.label: Dark greens, corn, egg yolks
eye-food.say: Dark leafy greens, corn, and egg yolks already contain lutein naturally. Getting it at the table is the sensible route, and it doesn't cost you anything extra.

eye-normalize.label: This is ordinary aging
eye-normalize.say: Cataracts are one of the most ordinary parts of getting older — clouding of the lens catches up with nearly everyone eventually. It isn't a sign that your health is worse than anyone else's.

eye-lutein.label: Lutein supplements
eye-lutein.dailyCap: Follow the product label; don't double up with another product containing the same ingredient
eye-lutein.say: Lutein does have real research behind it for protecting the macula — but here's the part people misread: **there's no evidence it reverses a cataract you already have.** It's protection, not treatment, so don't expect your vision to clear up. Greens, corn, and egg yolks have it already. **If you're on a blood thinner or you have surgery coming up, ask your doctor first** — and it's an ask-first during pregnancy or nursing too.

eye-surgery-blocked.label: Cataract surgery
eye-surgery-blocked.say: Whether to have cataract surgery, and when, is a medical judgment for the eye doctor. I won't make that call for you.

eye-refer.label: The eye problems that can't wait
eye-refer.say: **Sudden** loss of vision, a piece missing out of your field of view, a curtain coming down over one eye, or real pain in the eye — don't sit on any of those. Get seen the same day, at an eye doctor or the emergency room. Those can mean acute glaucoma or a detached retina, and neither one can be filed under 'my eyes are just getting older.'

itch-shower-temp.label: Turn the shower down
itch-shower-temp.say: Hot water feels wonderful and strips the oil right out of your skin — you come out itchier than you went in. Turn the temperature down and keep it shorter. Of everything here, this is the one you'll notice fastest.

itch-moisturize.label: Lotion while you're still damp
itch-moisturize.say: Put the lotion on while your skin is still damp from the shower — that's what seals the water in. Waiting until you're bone dry works far less well.

itch-clothes.label: Loose cotton next to the skin
itch-clothes.say: Loose cotton against the skin. Wool and rough fabrics rub all day long, and the rubbing is what feeds the itch.

itch-humidity.label: Don't let the air get too dry
itch-humidity.say: Heat in the winter and air conditioning in the summer both wring the moisture out of the air. A humidifier, or even a pan of water near the vent, makes your skin a good deal more comfortable.

itch-normalize.label: It comes with the years
itch-normalize.say: As we get older the skin makes less oil and holds water poorly, so itchy skin in later life is extremely common. It doesn't mean there's something wrong with you.

itch-steroid-blocked.label: Steroid creams
itch-steroid-blocked.say: I can't tell you which steroid cream to use or how to put it on — that depends on where it is and how bad it is, and it's a question for your doctor or pharmacist.

itch-refer.label: When itching is a signal
itch-refer.say: If the itching comes with yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes, weight you're losing without trying, or swollen glands — or if it keeps you awake at night, or you've scratched until the skin is broken and weeping — see a dermatologist. That can be a sign of something going on in the liver or kidneys, or an infection, rather than plain dry skin.

keywords: have to go all the time

noct-fluid-timing.label: Move the water earlier in the day
noct-fluid-timing.say: You don't need to drink less overall — just move it earlier. Ease off in the two or three hours before bed and make it up during the day. That alone usually takes a trip or two out of the night.

noct-caffeine-alcohol.label: Evening coffee and alcohol
noct-caffeine-alcohol.say: Coffee, strong tea, and alcohol all pull water straight out of you. In the evening, those are the first ones to go.

noct-night-safety.label: Make the trip to the bathroom safe
noct-night-safety.say: Nighttime is when falls happen. Put a night light along the path to the bathroom, keep the floor clear, and sit on the edge of the bed a moment before you stand up.

noct-normalize.label: Very common, nothing to be shy about
noct-normalize.say: Prostate trouble is one of the most ordinary parts of getting older for men — extremely common, and nothing to feel awkward about raising with a doctor.

noct-saw-palmetto.label: Saw palmetto and prostate supplements
noct-saw-palmetto.dailyCap: Follow the product label, and never add it on top of a prescription prostate medicine on your own
noct-saw-palmetto.say: Saw palmetto and the rest of that shelf have generally weak evidence — most trials haven't beaten a sugar pill — so I won't be the one recommending it. **And if you're already on a prescription prostate medicine, or a blood thinner, or you have surgery coming up, ask your pharmacist before you add anything.**

noct-dx-blocked.label: Is it harmless or is it something else
noct-dx-blocked.say: Whether this is a harmless enlargement or something else, I won't judge — that takes a urologist and an actual examination.

noct-refer.label: The ones that are emergencies
noct-refer.say: **If you can't pass urine at all, if there's blood in it, or you have severe pain in your side along with a fever — that's an emergency. Get seen right now; the emergency room is the right place for it.** And one more thing worth knowing: getting up at night is sometimes blood sugar or the heart sending up a flare. If your ankles swell or you're getting short of breath too, bring that up with your doctor at the same time.

reflux-no-lie-down.label: Don't lie down right after eating
reflux-no-lie-down.say: Stay upright for two or three hours after a meal, and try not to eat anything in the last three hours before bed. Of everything on this list, this is the one you'll feel the most.

reflux-late-dinner.label: Skip the late-night eating
reflux-late-dinner.say: Eating late and heading straight for the couch or bed is the classic heartburn recipe. If dinner has to be late, keep it small, skip the fried stuff, and give yourself a couple of hours before lying down.

reflux-raise-head.label: Raise the head of the bed
reflux-raise-head.say: Raise the head end of your bed six to eight inches — blocks or risers under the bed legs, or a wedge pillow. Stacking regular pillows doesn't do it; the whole upper body needs the slope. It keeps the acid downhill while you sleep.

reflux-diet.label: Less fried, less overstuffed
reflux-diet.say: Fried food, rich desserts, coffee, strong tea, and alcohol all invite the acid up. Trim those first, and stop eating before you're stuffed — an overfull stomach pushes back.

reflux-weight.label: Weight makes a real difference
reflux-weight.say: Pressure around the middle squeezes the stomach upward, so losing even some weight genuinely helps heartburn. No rush — slow and steady is fine.

reflux-meds-blocked.label: Heartburn medicines
reflux-meds-blocked.say: I can't tell you which heartburn medicine to take — and the over-the-counter acid reducers on every drugstore shelf aren't meant to be a long-term habit without a doctor involved. If you've been taking one for a long while, don't just quit on your own either; let your doctor decide.

reflux-refer.label: When to see a doctor — and when it's the heart
reflux-refer.say: If food is getting hard to swallow, you're losing weight without trying, or your stools turn black — see a doctor and get the stomach checked. **And the big one: heartburn can mask a heart attack. If it comes with a cold sweat, shortness of breath, pain spreading to the left arm or jaw, or it gets worse when you move around — treat it as your heart and call 911.**

reflux-left-side.label: Sleep on your left side
reflux-left-side.say: Sleep **on your left side**. This isn't folklore — it's been measured with probes overnight. Lying on the left, acid spends the least time in the esophagus; on the right, the most; on your back, in between. Left side also clears acid back down fastest. The practical trick is a body pillow behind your back — people roll flat once they're asleep, so you need something to hold the position. Honestly, it isn't like a medication that works within the hour; it's the "fewer bad nights" level of help. But it's free, and you can try it tonight.

reflux-after-meal-walk.label: Walk 10 to 15 minutes after eating, or chew sugar-free gum
reflux-after-meal-walk.say: Don't sit down with your phone after a meal — get up and walk slowly for 10 to 15 minutes. Researchers compared "walk after eating" with "chew sugar-free gum" while measuring esophageal acid, and both genuinely brought it down. **In the group chewing gum for 30 minutes after a meal, acid exposure time dropped by over 30%** — chewing keeps saliva flowing, saliva neutralizes acid, and it makes you swallow. Walking has a bonus for anyone who bloats: the gas moves along. Just walk — no brisk pace to breathlessness, and nothing that compresses the belly like sit-ups right after eating.

reflux-small-meals.label: Stop at about three-quarters full, eat smaller and more often, slow down
reflux-small-meals.say: Stop at about three-quarters full and eat four or five smaller meals instead of three big ones. Overfilling raises pressure in the stomach and the valve at the bottom of the esophagus can't hold. Then **slow down**: chew more per bite, don't talk through a mouthful, skip straws, cut back on carbonated drinks. All of that is about swallowing less air. About half of what people call bloating is swallowed air. One commonly missed piece: **if dentures don't fit or chewing is hard, food gets gulped down whole** — fix the teeth first, because changing how you eat won't get around that.

reflux-belt-bend.label: Loosen the belt, don't bend or lift right after eating
reflux-belt-bend.say: Let the belt out a notch and stop cinching the waistband — you feel this one immediately. A tight waist is constant upward pressure on the stomach. For an hour or two after eating, don't bend forward: no scrubbing the floor on your knees, no lifting anything heavy, no leaning into the dryer. To pick something up, bend the knees and keep the back straight. And smoking loosens that valve at the bottom of the esophagus — there's no compromise version of that one. If quitting isn't happening yet, cutting five cigarettes a day is still better than doing nothing.

reflux-gas-foods.label: Bloating — find the one or two things making the gas
reflux-gas-foods.say: If you're passing a lot of gas and the belly feels tight, check whether these are in your daily rotation: cabbage, cauliflower, broccoli, brussels sprouts, onions, garlic, asparagus; beans, lentils, soy; sweet potato, corn, and sugar-free products with sorbitol or xylitol; and anything carbonated. None of these are bad foods and you don't need to drop them all. **Remove one at a time for a week or two** and find the actual one or two culprits. Then go back to eating the rest. Cooking matters too — soak beans before cooking, cook vegetables softer. Easier going through than raw and crunchy.

reflux-milk-lactose.label: Bloated after milk? Test for lactose intolerance first
reflux-milk-lactose.say: If the bloating or the run to the bathroom follows milk or a powdered nutrition drink, lactose intolerance is a strong bet. It's very common in adults worldwide, and **it's a trait, not a damaged gut.** Testing is simple: drop all dairy for two weeks. If things clearly improve, have a glass again — if the bloating comes back, you have your answer. You don't have to give up dairy forever: switch to lactose-free milk, try yogurt or hard cheese, drink it with food, or have half a cup at a time. Most people find a level that works. Just replace the calcium elsewhere — canned sardines, tofu, dark leafy greens, fortified alternatives.

reflux-breathing.label: Diaphragmatic breathing (worth doing, but not the main event)
reflux-breathing.say: You can practice this. Lying down or sitting, one hand on the chest and one on the belly, breathe in slowly through the nose so the belly rises and the chest stays still, then breathe out longer than you breathed in. Five to ten minutes, twice a day, at least an hour after eating. The idea is to strengthen the diaphragm, which wraps right around the valve at the bottom of the esophagus. Honestly: pooling the small trials, symptom scores do improve, but the methods vary a lot and the conclusion isn't settled. It's free and harmless, so treat it as a side dish — but don't let it replace the items above.

reflux-ginger.label: Ginger (there's research behind it, but three groups should ask first)
reflux-ginger.dailyCap: Up to 4 g a day total — roughly three or four thin slices
reflux-ginger.say: Ginger is one of the few foods in this topic with research behind it. Pooled trials show it beats placebo for upper-belly fullness and early satiety, and it genuinely speeds stomach emptying. Steep it as tea or cook with it — **up to 4 grams a day total**, about three or four thin slices. Three groups should check with a doctor or pharmacist first: anyone on a blood thinner, anyone with gallstones, and anyone with surgery within two weeks. And if heartburn is your main symptom rather than fullness, ginger makes some people burn more. Don't push it.

reflux-supplement-skip.label: Are the "stomach support" supplements worth buying?
reflux-supplement-skip.dailyCap: Not recommended for this. Avoid long-term use of anything containing licorice
reflux-supplement-skip.say: People ask about the stomach-support supplements — licorice extract (DGL), aloe vera juice, melatonin and similar. Honestly: **in people with reflux these have only small or preliminary studies behind them, nothing large or solid. The effect isn't dependable.** Keep your money for now. The items we covered — losing weight, nothing to eat in the two or three hours before bed, raising the head of the bed 6 to 8 inches, sleeping on the left — have far stronger evidence, cost nothing, and work every night. One caution: **licorice in quantity raises blood pressure and drops potassium.** That matters especially if you have high blood pressure, poor kidney function, or take a diuretic.

vax-free-eligibility.label: On Medicare, these mostly cost you nothing
vax-free-eligibility.say: Good news on the money side: if you're on Medicare, the shots older adults need mostly cost nothing out of pocket. **Part B covers the flu shot, the pneumonia shots, and COVID-19 with no cost-sharing at all. Shingles and RSV run through your Part D drug plan — and since the law changed, those are $0 too, as long as you use a pharmacy or provider inside your plan's network.** Your regular pharmacy can usually give all of them and look up what you're due for. Do check the network part first — that's where the surprise bills come from.

vax-why.label: Why it matters more as we age
vax-why.say: As we get older the immune system doesn't answer as quickly, so flu and pneumonia are likelier to turn serious and drag complications behind them. A shot isn't a promise you won't get sick — it's about pushing down the odds of ending up in the hospital.

vax-side-effects.label: The honest word on side effects
vax-side-effects.say: The usual is a sore arm for a day or two, and some people run a mild fever or feel wiped out. It generally passes quickly — not the horror stories that get passed around, but not nothing either. The shingles shot in particular has a reputation for a rough day afterward, so it's worth planning a quiet day rather than being taken by surprise.

vax-eligibility-blocked.label: Whether you're in shape for it today
vax-eligibility-blocked.say: Whether you're in shape for a shot right now — running a fever, immune problems, an allergy to something in it — is the doctor's or the pharmacist's judgment, not mine. Mention anything like that before they draw it up.

vax-refer.label: The rare reaction that can't wait
vax-refer.say: If after a shot you have trouble breathing, your face or throat starts to swell, or you break out in hives all over — **that's a severe allergic reaction. Call 911 right away. Don't drive yourself, and don't wait to see whether it settles.** It's rare, and it's the one thing here you should never sit on.

swallow-texture.label: Change how the food is made, not what it is
swallow-texture.say: Cut things smaller, cook them softer, and add a little sauce or gravy so the food slides instead of catching. Same dinner — it just goes down far more easily.

swallow-thin-liquid.label: Thin liquids are the hardest, not the easiest
swallow-thin-liquid.say: This one surprises people: thin liquids are harder to swallow safely, not easier. Plain water catches folks more often than anything else on the table. If water keeps going down the wrong way, ask a speech therapist whether a thickener would help.

swallow-pace.label: Small bites, sitting up, no talking
swallow-pace.say: Small bites, chew well, sit up straight, and try not to talk while you're eating. Those few habits by themselves cut the choking down a great deal.

swallow-eval.label: Get a proper swallow evaluation
swallow-eval.say: If choking is happening regularly, the most useful thing you can do is get a proper swallow evaluation — a speech-language pathologist or an ENT doctor. Your primary care doctor can put in the referral, and with a doctor's order it's usually covered. Changing the food is a help, not a substitute for having it looked at.

swallow-normalize.label: More common than people realize
swallow-normalize.say: Chewing and swallowing getting harder is very common in later life — especially for people living in nursing homes or assisted living. It isn't a sign that you're becoming useless.

swallow-dental-blocked.label: Dentures and implants
swallow-dental-blocked.say: Whether to get dentures or implants, and which kind, is the dentist's judgment. I won't decide that one for you.

swallow-refer.label: Choking right now, and what needs an appointment
swallow-refer.say: **If someone is choking right this moment — can't speak, can't breathe, turning blue — call 911 and start abdominal thrusts, the Heimlich, immediately.** That moment is not one that 'cut it smaller and eat slowly' can fix. Separately: if choking keeps happening, or weight is dropping fast, ask the doctor for a swallow evaluation.

mci-normalize-vs-warn.label: Ordinary forgetting versus the kind to watch
mci-normalize-vs-warn.say: Blanking on a name, or forgetting where you set the keys but remembering as soon as someone jogs you — that's more like ordinary aging. What's worth paying attention to is losing the whole event, asking the same question over and over, or getting lost somewhere you know well.

mci-exercise.label: Exercise has the strongest evidence
mci-exercise.say: When it comes to protecting the brain, exercise has the strongest evidence of anything — stronger than any brain supplement on the shelf. A brisk walk a few times a week counts.

mci-social.label: People and new things
mci-social.say: Conversation, cards, learning something new, the senior center, church — being around people and using your head helps slow things down, and it works better than sitting at home alone with a book of puzzles.

mci-hearing-vision.label: Get the hearing and the eyes seen to
mci-hearing-vision.say: This one gets skipped far too often: not hearing well and not seeing well make people pull back and stop going out — and hearing loss is one of the few dementia risk factors you can genuinely do something about. If you need hearing aids or your eyes checked, go get it done. Hearing aids are sold over the counter now for mild to moderate loss, which has brought the price down a lot.

mci-vascular.label: Blood pressure and blood sugar are brain care
mci-vascular.say: Keeping blood pressure, blood sugar, and cholesterol in line is brain protection — the brain runs on those blood vessels. That, not a supplement, is what looks after your memory.

mci-brain-supp.label: Ginkgo and the brain supplements
mci-brain-supp.dailyCap: Follow the product label; don't double up with other products of the same kind
mci-brain-supp.say: Straight answer on ginkgo and the memory-supplement aisle: the evidence that any of it prevents or slows memory decline is generally not there. I'd rather you didn't put your money or your hopes on that shelf. Exercise, keeping blood pressure and blood sugar in line, and staying around people have far clearer evidence behind them. If you want to try one anyway — **ginkgo raises bleeding risk, so if you take a blood thinner or aspirin, or you have surgery coming up, ask your doctor first.**

mci-checkup.label: Get it properly evaluated
mci-checkup.say: Rather than guessing at home, get it evaluated — your primary care doctor, a neurologist, or a memory clinic. **And here's a practical one: Medicare's yearly Wellness Visit already includes a memory check, at no cost to you** — you can ask for it by name. It matters because some memory trouble turns out to be thyroid, low B12, depression, or a medication — and every one of those is fixable.

mci-dementia-drug-blocked.label: Dementia medications
mci-dementia-drug-blocked.say: Whether to use a dementia medication, and which one, comes after a doctor's evaluation. That isn't a judgment I'll make.

mci-refer.label: Sudden confusion is a different thing entirely
mci-refer.say: **If confusion comes on suddenly — over hours, or a day or two — not recognizing people, speech coming out jumbled: that isn't dementia. That's delirium, and it's often an infection or a medication behind it. Get seen right away, today, not next week.** The slow kind — getting lost on familiar roads, asking the same thing over and over, a real change in personality — is what a memory clinic evaluation is for.

cramp-stretch-before-bed.label: Stretch the calf before bed
cramp-stretch-before-bed.say: Before bed, stand facing a wall with the back leg straight and the heel down, and hold that calf stretch about thirty seconds — two or three times. For night cramps this is one of the few things with actual research behind it.

cramp-hydration.label: Water through the day
cramp-hydration.say: The days that catch you are the ones where you sweated a lot or drank too little. Top the water up across the day rather than gulping a glass at bedtime.

cramp-warm.label: Warm feet cramp less
cramp-warm.say: Cold feet cramp more easily. A warm foot soak before bed and keeping your feet covered under the blankets — there's no downside to it, and plenty of people say it makes a real difference.

cramp-food-minerals.label: Minerals from food
cramp-food-minerals.say: Bananas, leafy greens, nuts, beans, milk and yogurt — potassium, magnesium and calcium from the table beat buying another bottle.

cramp-magnesium.label: Magnesium supplements
cramp-magnesium.dailyCap: No more than 350 mg a day from supplements (the U.S. safe upper limit)
cramp-magnesium.say: Magnesium gets recommended for cramps constantly, so here's the honest version: **in trials on older adults with night cramps, most didn't show a clear benefit** — the evidence looks better for cramps in pregnancy. You can try it; just don't pin high hopes on it. **If your kidneys aren't in good shape, don't start it on your own**, and it has to be spaced apart from certain antibiotics and osteoporosis medicines, so ask your pharmacist. Keep supplements at or under 350 mg a day — that's the U.S. safe ceiling, and more than that mostly buys you diarrhea.

cramp-med-review.label: It might be one of your medicines
cramp-med-review.say: Some water pills and cholesterol medicines make cramps more likely. If these started up after a medication change, mention it at your next visit and let the doctor look — **but never stop anything on your own.**

cramp-quinine-blocked.label: Quinine for cramps
cramp-quinine-blocked.say: There's an old remedy for cramps — quinine — that I won't help you get hold of. **The FDA has warned more than once that using it for leg cramps isn't worth the risk: the serious reactions include a dangerous drop in platelets and kidney damage, and deaths have been reported.** It's approved for malaria, not for this. Tonic water gets suggested for the same reason, and that isn't a plan either.

cramp-refer.label: When it isn't an ordinary cramp
cramp-refer.say: If one calf stays swollen, hot and painful, that one needs a doctor promptly so a blood clot can be ruled out. Same if the cramping comes with weakness or numbness, or if your legs ache after walking a certain distance and you have to stop and rest. Those aren't ordinary cramps.

supp-inventory.label: List everything you take
supp-inventory.say: Let's make one list of everything — prescriptions, vitamins, supplements, the ones you take daily and the ones you take when you remember. Just seeing it all in one place, people usually spot the doubles themselves.

supp-red-yeast.label: Red yeast rice + statins is a real risk
supp-red-yeast.dailyCap: Follow the product label — and never combine it with a statin without asking your doctor or pharmacist first
supp-red-yeast.say: Here's the one that matters most: red yeast rice naturally contains the same kind of compound as statin drugs. Taking it alongside a prescription statin doubles up the load and risks serious muscle damage. If you're on both, don't decide anything yourself — take both bottles to your pharmacist and ask.

supp-grapefruit.label: Grapefruit makes some medicines too strong
supp-grapefruit.say: This one surprises a lot of people: **grapefruit — including grapefruit juice at breakfast — blocks the enzyme your liver uses to break down certain medicines, so the drug builds up stronger than intended**. Statins, some blood pressure pills, and some sleep medicines are on the list, and **the effect lasts two or three days, so spacing them apart doesn't help**. If you take any regular medication, ask your pharmacist 'is grapefruit okay with my pills?' before making it a habit. Pomelo does the same thing.

supp-food-first.label: Food before pills, always
supp-food-first.say: Whatever you can get from real food, get from real food. Supplements are for filling genuine gaps — they're not a substitute for eating well.

supp-ask-pharmacist.label: Take the whole bag to your pharmacist
supp-ask-pharmacist.say: Once your list is made, here's the most practical step: bring the whole bag — pills, vitamins, everything — to your pharmacy and ask for a medication review. Pharmacists do this all the time, and if you're on a Medicare drug plan you may qualify for a free yearly review (it's called Medication Therapy Management — just ask). They can spot two bottles that fight each other at a glance.

supp-normalize.label: A drawer full is normal
supp-normalize.say: About seven in ten older Americans take at least one supplement — a crowded medicine cabinet is completely normal, not a sign you've been foolish with your money.

supp-no-brand-blocked.label: Brands, doses, and 'is it safe with my meds'
supp-no-brand-blocked.say: I won't recommend specific brands or ingredients, I don't give doses, and I won't be the one to tell you 'that's fine with your medications' — that judgment belongs to your pharmacist, who can actually see the whole picture.

supp-refer.label: When to stop and get help
supp-refer.say: If after starting any supplement you get muscle pain or weakness, your skin or the whites of your eyes turn yellow, or your heart starts racing — stop taking it and get medical help promptly. That's not a wait-and-see situation.

osteo-fall-proof-home.label: Clear the falls out of the house tonight
osteo-fall-proof-home.say: What's really dangerous about thin bones is the fall. Tonight's list: a non-slip mat in the tub, nothing left lying in the walkways, cords tucked out of the path, and a night light between the bed and the bathroom. Throw rugs are the worst offender of all — either tape them down or get rid of them.

osteo-strength-balance.label: Balance and leg strength
osteo-strength-balance.say: Stand on one leg holding the back of a chair. Practice getting up out of a chair and back down. And look into tai chi — a lot of senior centers teach it. For preventing falls, the evidence behind balance and leg strength is stronger than the evidence for calcium.

osteo-sunlight.label: Daylight, and walk while you're out
osteo-sunlight.say: Fifteen or twenty minutes outside most days, and walk while you're at it. That's the cheapest vitamin D there is.

osteo-calcium-food.label: Calcium from food
osteo-calcium-food.say: Milk and yogurt, canned sardines or salmon with the bones still in, tofu, leafy greens, almonds and sesame — calcium from food absorbs best, and it doesn't carry the kidney stone worry.

osteo-calcium-vitd-supp.label: Calcium with vitamin D
osteo-calcium-vitd-supp.dailyCap: For adults over 50, keep total calcium — food plus pills together — at or under about 2,000 mg a day; that's a safety ceiling, not a target
osteo-calcium-vitd-supp.say: If food honestly isn't getting you there, calcium with vitamin D is a reasonable way to fill the gap — with three things to remember. **Split it into smaller doses rather than one big one**, because you absorb more that way. **Don't start it on your own if you've had kidney stones, high calcium, or a parathyroid problem.** And it has to be spaced apart from osteoporosis and thyroid medicines. How much, and whether you need it at all — take your current pill bottles in and ask your doctor or pharmacist.

osteo-quit-smoke-alcohol.label: Smoking and drinking cost you bone
osteo-quit-smoke-alcohol.say: Smoking and drinking both speed bone loss along. Cutting back on either one does more for your bones than another bottle of calcium ever will.

osteo-dexa.label: Get a bone density scan
osteo-dexa.say: Rather than wondering, get a bone density scan — a DXA. It's quick and it's painless. **Medicare Part B covers one every two years for people who qualify, at no cost to you** — being an older woman at risk, or having been on steroids for months, are the kinds of things that qualify. Ask your primary care doctor whether you're eligible.

osteo-meds-blocked.label: Osteoporosis medications
osteo-meds-blocked.say: Whether to be on an osteoporosis medicine — the pills or the injections — and which one, is the doctor's decision based on your bone density and your fracture risk. I won't judge that for you.

osteo-refer.label: After a fall, and the signs of a spine fracture
osteo-refer.say: **If someone falls and can't get up, or the pain is bad enough that they can't move — don't haul them up yourself. Call 911 and let them do it.** Moving a broken hip the wrong way makes it worse. Separately: getting noticeably shorter, hunching over faster than before, or sudden back pain can mean a fracture in the spine — that one needs a doctor.

mood-listen-first.label: Being heard comes first
mood-listen-first.say: We don't have to fix anything right now. If you feel like talking, I'm listening — saying this stuff out loud genuinely helps, all by itself.

mood-daylight-walk.label: Daylight and a walk
mood-daylight-walk.say: A twenty-minute walk outside in the daylight — for mild to moderate low mood, exercise has real research behind it. That's not a pep talk; it's one of the best-proven things there is.

mood-one-connection.label: See someone once a week
mood-one-connection.say: Too much time alone pulls the mood downward. One real get-together a week is enough to push back — an old friend, church, the senior center, coffee with a neighbor. Anything counts.

mood-sleep-link.label: Check the sleep side first
mood-sleep-link.say: Bad sleep and low mood are usually two sides of the same coin. Sort out the sleep first, and the mood often loosens its grip a little on its own.

mood-caregiver-respite.label: Caregivers need relief too
mood-caregiver-respite.say: You're not failing — you're running on empty, and you have been for a while. Respite care exists exactly for this: someone takes over for a few hours so you can breathe. Call the Eldercare Locator at 1-800-677-1116 (weekdays) and ask what's available near you. Taking a break is not quitting.

mood-1925.label: The 988 Lifeline — someone to talk to, day or night
mood-1925.say: If the nights are the hardest part — 988 is the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline. It's free, it's there 24/7, and you can call **or text** the same three digits. You don't have to be in crisis to reach out; feeling awful is reason enough.

mood-antidep-blocked.label: Antidepressants
mood-antidep-blocked.say: Whether to take an antidepressant, and which one, is a decision for a doctor — and if you're already on one, never stop it cold on your own; coming off suddenly can feel terrible. That's a conversation with your prescriber.

mood-refer.label: When to reach out for real help
mood-refer.say: If you're having thoughts of hurting yourself, or life has started to feel like it's not worth living — call or text 988 right now, or call 911, and let someone close to you know. And if it's been two weeks or more of barely eating, barely sleeping, nothing bringing any interest — that's depression, a medical condition, not a character flaw. It deserves a doctor the same way a broken arm does.

cold-ask-pharmacist.label: Ask the pharmacist before you take anything
cold-ask-pharmacist.say: Here's the line that matters most on this one: **the multi-symptom cold medicines in your cabinet mix badly with prescriptions.** Two things in particular — most of them already contain acetaminophen, so it's easy to double up without meaning to, and the decongestant in them can push your blood pressure up. Before you take any of it, hold the box up at the pharmacy counter and ask, 'does this fight with what I'm on?' It takes a minute. One more piece of honesty while we're here: **the FDA has proposed pulling oral phenylephrine — the decongestant in a lot of those boxes — because its review found it doesn't actually work when you swallow it.**

cold-rest-fluids.label: Fluids and sleep
cold-rest-fluids.say: Most ordinary colds are a virus. Fluids and sleep, and the symptoms generally ease off over about a week. Antibiotics do nothing for a virus, which is worth knowing before you go asking for them.

cold-protect-others.label: Don't hand it to the household
cold-protect-others.say: Wash your hands and wear a mask around others — especially if there's an older person or a small child in the house. For you it's a rotten few days; passing it to someone frail can mean a hospital stay.

cold-warm-fluids.label: Warm things for the throat
cold-warm-fluids.say: Warm water, broth, tea with honey — it makes the throat feel better. **(Never honey for a baby under a year old.)** This is comfort rather than cure, and there's nothing wrong with that.

cold-otc-blocked.label: Brands and doses
cold-otc-blocked.say: I won't name a brand or tell you how much to take, and I won't be the one to say whether this is a cold, the flu, or pneumonia — that needs a doctor.

cold-refer.label: When it's stopped being just a cold
cold-refer.say: A fever that won't break after three days, getting short of breath, someone acting confused or not themselves, or a chronic condition clearly getting worse — at that point it isn't a cold you ride out at home. Call the doctor.

palp-record.label: Write down what it did
palp-record.say: Next time it happens, jot down four things: when it started, how long it went on, whether you felt dizzy or tight in the chest, and what you were doing at the time. A cardiologist can do a great deal with notes like that — far more than with 'it happens sometimes.'

palp-caffeine.label: See whether it's the caffeine
palp-caffeine.say: Coffee, strong tea, energy drinks, and being short on sleep all make your heartbeat more noticeable. Cut one of them for a week and see whether anything changes.

palp-anxiety.label: Nerves set it off too
palp-anxiety.say: Palpitations often ride along with anxiety rather than coming from the heart itself. When it starts, sit down and breathe out slowly and long — don't jump up and start moving around.

palp-anemia.label: It can also be anemia
palp-anemia.say: Sometimes a racing heart turns out to be anemia, especially in women. Ask to have that looked at next time you're having blood drawn.

palp-normalize.label: Common as we age
palp-normalize.say: Irregular heartbeats become more common as we get older. Being frightened by them is a perfectly normal reaction — and not every kind is dangerous.

palp-dx-blocked.label: Harmless or dangerous
palp-dx-blocked.say: Whether this is a harmless rhythm or a dangerous one, I can't judge at all — that's a medical diagnosis. What I can do is help you keep the record, and go with you to the appointment.

palp-refer.label: When it's 911
palp-refer.say: **If the palpitations come with chest pain, trouble breathing, fainting, a cold sweat, or pain spreading into your left arm or jaw — call 911. Right then, not after waiting to see.** And because some rhythm problems raise the risk of stroke: a drooping face, a weak arm, or slurred speech is 911 as well, immediately.

neck-strength-training.label: Strength beats stretching
neck-strength-training.say: Here's a finding that runs against instinct — what actually helps most is **strengthening**, not endless stretching. Shoulder shrugs, a rowing motion with a band, standing tall against a wall. A few times a week does more than stretching every single day.

neck-workstation.label: Fix the chair, desk and screen
neck-workstation.say: Screen at eye level, feet flat on the floor, elbows supported. In the research, fixing the setup and doing the strength work together beat either one on its own — and the setup you can fix this afternoon.

neck-microbreak.label: Get up every hour
neck-microbreak.say: Set a timer: once an hour, stand up, walk for a minute, roll the shoulders. What wrecks you isn't so much bad posture as holding any one posture too long.

neck-heat.label: A heating pad
neck-heat.say: A heating pad when it's really aching does make the evening easier. That's relief, not a repair — and relief still counts.

neck-gentle-yoga.label: Stretching and yoga
neck-gentle-yoga.say: Stretching and yoga feel good and do help — the research behind them just isn't as solid as it is for strength work. Wonderful for loosening up; don't let it be the only thing you do.

neck-caregiver-transfer.label: Lifting someone without wrecking your back
neck-caregiver-transfer.say: When you help someone up, bend your knees, bring them close to you first, and lift with your legs — not by bending over and taking it all in your back. Caregivers' back injuries get built one lift at a time. And ask about equipment: your local Area Agency on Aging, reachable through the Eldercare Locator at 1-800-677-1116 on weekdays, can tell you about loan programs, and some equipment is covered by Medicare when a doctor prescribes it.

neck-refer.label: When to stop toughing it out
neck-refer.say: If your hand goes numb or weak, if the pain is bad enough to keep you awake, or if it runs down your arm — get it looked at. Start with your primary care doctor, who can send you on to physical therapy or an orthopedist. Don't just grit your teeth through it month after month.

teen-explain-biology.label: It's biology, not laziness
teen-explain-biology.say: Arguing about bedtime usually goes nowhere, because at that age the body genuinely isn't ready for sleep yet — through the teen years the sleep signal shifts a couple of hours later. Teenagers need somewhere between eight and ten hours and most are running on closer to seven. So skip the fight over lights-out, and put the effort into mornings and weekends instead.

teen-weekend-anchor.label: Weekends are where it unravels
